STEP 1 - Scene: Two slices of pepperoni pizza (thin-to-medium crust, tomato sauce, melted cheese, pepperoni) on a white plate. Only the two slices are part of this meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square-ish plate with rounded corners, roughly 26 cm across (dinner plate). Area = 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) pizza slice, left; (b) pizza slice, right, with a bit of crust. Visible sauce and cheese are part of the slices. A few crumbs are negligible.

STEP 4 - Area: The two slices together cover roughly 15% of the plate (left slice ~8%, right slice ~7%).

STEP 5 - Volume: Each slice is a thin wedge, about 1.5 to 2 cm tall at the crust, tapering. Left slice ~42 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 63 ml; right slice ~37 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 55 ml. Total ≈ 118 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Pizza slices are bread-like, density ~0.9 g/ml. Total ≈ 106 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Pizza with cheese and pepperoni is about 270-290 kcal per 100 g. Using 280 kcal/100 g: 106 g x 2.8 ≈ 297 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two medium slices of pizza weigh around 200 g in typical restaurant form, but these slices look thinner and smaller than a full restaurant slice and only partly fill the plate. About 106 g is plausible for what is visible, and roughly 300 kcal fits. The estimate may be low if the slices are denser than assumed, so the true range is perhaps 100 to 150 g.
